name: Triose Phosphate-Isomerase Deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly reduced triose phosphate isomerase enzyme activity in erythrocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TPI1 gene by molecular genetic testing
Presence of chronic hemolytic anemia with neuromuscular symptoms including progressive muscle weakness and neurodegeneration
Elevated serum lactate and evidence of hemolysis (e.g., elevated reticulocyte count, low haptoglobin)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Reduced TPI enzyme activity and identification of pathogenic TPI1 mutations along with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be confirmed by enzyme assay and genetic testing; clinical presentation is typically severe infantile-onset hemolytic anemia with neuromuscular involvement.

laboratory: Markedly reduced triose phosphate isomerase enzyme activity in erythrocytes
Evidence of hemolysis: elevated reticulocytes, low haptoglobin, elevated indirect bilirubin
imaging: MRI brain may show cerebral atrophy and white matter changes
other: Muscle biopsy may show neurogenic atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Pyruvate kinase deficiency presents with hemolytic anemia but lacks neuromuscular degeneration
Enzyme assay shows normal TPI activity
Glycogen storage disease type VII (Tarui disease) presents with muscle weakness and hemolysis but involves phosphofructokinase deficiency
Different genetic mutations and enzyme assays

redFlags: Failure to thrive with metabolic acidosis
references: Saudubray JM, et al. Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment. 6th ed. Springer; 2016.
